subtitle: How Forts, Forests and Eighty-Four Villages Held a Kingdom Together

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a forested hill-fort rising above dense teak and river mist
panels.action: The Gond Clan Chief of a Garh stands on a stone rampart above a maze of green valleys and scattered villages, his spear grounded beside him, as winding forest paths and distant watch-fires hint at a hidden system.

dialogue.text: In Garha-Katanga’s dark forests, Gond clan chiefs built a quiet machine of forts, eighty-four-village circles and twelve-village chains—an unseen code that held elephants, iron and people together.

i18n.hi: गढ़ा-कटंग के अँधेरे जंगलों में गोंड सरदारों ने चुपचाप जाल बुना—किलों, चौरासी गाँवों और बारह गाँवों की कड़ियों का, एक अदृश्य कोड जो हाथी, लोहा और लोग जोड़े रखता था।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view drifting over a map-like landscape
panels.action: From high above, the land of Garha-Katanga spreads out like a living map: forested ridges, rivers, scattered clearings and hilltop forts, with faint paths linking clusters of huts and smoke rising in tiny spirals.

dialogue.text: Colonial gazetteers later saw only scattered forests and ‘backward’ villages here. Yet beneath this seeming looseness lay a pattern—garh, chaurasi, barhot—remembered in place-names and tribute lists.

i18n.hi: अंग्रेज़ों की गज़ेटियरों को यहाँ बस टुकड़ों में जंगल और ‘पिछड़े’ गाँव दिखे। पर इस ढीलेपन के नीचे था एक ढाँचा—गढ़, चौरासी, बारहट—जो जगहों के नाम और लगान सूचियों में बचा रहा।

panels.shot: medium shot of the chief in council inside a dim fort hall lit by oil lamps
panels.action: Inside a stone hall, the Gond Clan Chief sits cross-legged on a low platform, elders and hunters around him, a rough wooden board between them marked with pebbles and scratched circles for villages and paths.

dialogue.text: There was no neat written manual. What we know of this order comes from later records and memories. But the structure they describe is clear: forts as nodes, village clusters as rings around them.

i18n.hi: कोई साफ लिखित किताब नहीं थी। इस व्यवस्था की झलक हमें बाद के दस्तों और यादों से मिलती है। पर जो नज़ारा उभरता है, वह साफ है: किले धुरी, गाँवों के झुंड उनकी गोल चक्कर।

panels.shot: wide shot of a hill-fort dominating a valley
panels.action: A massive hill-fort crowns a spur above a river, its stone walls hugging the ridge, wooden gates flanked by watchtowers, with cattle, women at wells and children playing in the terraced fields below.

dialogue.text: The garh was not just a fort. It was a territory. A Gond clan chief held its walls, its water, its grazing hills, and the scattered hamlets that looked to its drums for warning and to its granaries in famine.

i18n.hi: गढ़ सिर्फ किला नहीं था, इलाक़ा था। गोंड सरदार उसकी दीवारें, पानी, चरागाह पहाड़ियाँ, और बिखरे टोलों को थामे रहते, जो खतरे पर उसकी नगाड़ों पर, और अकाल में उसकी कोठियों पर टिके थे।

panels.shot: slow push-in on the chief leaning on a parapet, watching distant villages
panels.action: Leaning on the parapet, the Gond Clan Chief peers across the valley at distant smoke from huts and glinting fields, his brow furrowed as he traces unseen lines between them in his mind.

dialogue.text: Around each garh spread its chaurasi—an eighty-four-village unit, as later people recalled it. Not a neat square on a clerk’s paper, but a loose ring of hamlets linked by forest paths, kinship and obligation.

i18n.hi: हर गढ़ के चारों ओर फैला उसका चौरासी—चौरासी गाँवों का घेरा, जैसा बाद के लोगों ने याद रखा। कोई मुंशी की सीधी चौखट नहीं, बल्कि जंगल-पगडंडियों, रिश्तों और फ़र्ज़ से जुड़ी ढीली माला।

panels.shot: diagrammatic wide shot: foreground chief, background landscape subtly grouped in clusters
panels.action: In the foreground the chief points with a staff; in the distance, the artist subtly groups villages into larger and smaller clusters along rivers and ridges, suggesting nested circles without any written marks.

dialogue.text: Within each eighty-four came smaller chains—the barhot, remembered as a twelve-village subdivision. A handful of clearings woven together so that forest, field and stream could be watched and shared.

i18n.hi: हर चौरासी के भीतर उतरते थे छोटे हलके—बारहट, जिन्हें बारह गाँवों के हिस्से के रूप में याद किया गया। कुछ खुलेखेत, जो मिलकर जंगल, खेत और नाले पर नज़र और बाँट को पक्का करते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a village clearing where the chief meets headmen
panels.action: In a sun-dappled clearing, village headmen with different tattoos and ornaments sit around the Gond Clan Chief; they bring baskets of grain, bundles of iron tools and a tethered elephant calf as offerings.

dialogue.text: Each level owed and received. Headmen of a barhot brought grain, iron, labour and sometimes elephant calves to the garh. In return, they gained protection, water rights, and a voice in the chief’s council.

i18n.hi: हर पायदान पर देना और लेना था। बारहट के मुंखियाँ गढ़ पर अनाज, लोहा, मज़दूरी और कभी-कभी हाथी के बच्चे लाते। बदले में उन्हें हिफ़ाज़त, पानी के हक़, और दरबार में बोलने की सीट मिलती।

panels.shot: low-angle close-up of an elephant’s eye with the chief’s reflection in it
panels.action: An elephant’s eye fills the frame, its skin wrinkled and dusty, the faint reflection of the Gond Clan Chief standing with mahouts, as forest trees blur behind them.

dialogue.text: Sumit Guha and others remind us: this was not a petty grain-state. Control of elephants, iron from forest smelters, timber and routes mattered as much as crops. The chaurasi system watched these veins.

i18n.hi: सुमित गुहा और दूसरे बताते हैं: यह कोई छोटा अनाज-राज नहीं था। हाथियों पर पकड़, जंगल भट्टियों का लोहा, लकड़ी और रास्ते, फसलों जितने अहम थे। चौरासी की जाँच इन्हीं नसों पर रहती थी।

panels.shot: wide shot of a river with ghats and irrigation channels below the fort
panels.action: Below the fort, a river bends; simple stone ghats lead down to the water, and crude wooden sluice gates divert streams into small fields, where farmers in loincloths and saris transplant seedlings.

dialogue.text: Water was the spine. A garh was sited near rivers and tanks. Barhots were strung along streams, so that one chief could open or close the flow with a word, and in drought, direct seed and grain where it mattered most.

i18n.hi: पानी इसकी रीढ़ था। गढ़ नदियों और तालों के पास बसते। बारहट नालों की धारा में पिरोए रहते, ताकि एक सरदार एक शब्द से पानी खोल-बंद कर सके, और सूखे में बीज और अनाज ठीक जगह मोड़ सके।

panels.shot: interior wide shot of the fort courtyard where armed men drill
panels.action: In the fort’s dusty courtyard, lean archers, spearmen and shield-bearers practice in ordered lines, while at the gate a messenger arrives, breathless, saluting the Gond Clan Chief with urgency.

dialogue.speaker: the_gond_clan_chiefs
dialogue.text: From each barhot, three men and one elephant—ready when the drum sounds.

i18n.hi: हर बारहट से, तीन मर्द और एक हाथी—नगाड़ा बजते ही तैयार।

panels.shot: medium shot of the chief facing a distant royal envoy on horseback
panels.action: On the fort’s approach road, a royal envoy in more ornate dress waits astride his horse, flanked by attendants; the Gond Clan Chief stands bareheaded before him, their eyes level but wary.

dialogue.text: Above the garh stood the raja of Garha-Katanga. Gazetteers recall how each fort-clan owed tribute upwards—grain, iron, men, elephants—yet kept its own council and forests. A federated web, not a neat pyramid.

i18n.hi: गढ़ के ऊपर बैठता था गढ़ा-कटंग का राजा। गज़ेटियर बताते हैं कि हर किला-कुल ऊपर को नज़राना देता—अनाज, लोहा, लोग, हाथी—पर अपना दरबार और जंगल अपने पास रखता। एक जाल, सीढ़ीनुमा राज नहीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of dense forest road with watch-posts and toll collectors
panels.action: On a narrow forest road, traders’ bullock carts inch between tall trees; at a rough wooden barrier, Gond guards with spears sit by a fire, weighing bundles and taking a small share as they lift the gate.

dialogue.text: Routes were arteries. Clan chiefs watched passes and river crossings, taking dues and keeping order. Their power lay as much in knowing every bend and hill as in any title the raja bestowed.

i18n.hi: राहें नसें थीं। कुल सरदार दर्रों और नदी-घाटों पर नज़र रखते, चुंगी लेते और क़ायदा रखते। उनकी ताक़त उतनी ही थी हर मोड़ और पहाड़ी को जानने में, जितनी किसी हुक्मनामा-शुदा औहदे में।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a nighttime council in the fort with torches and tension
panels.action: At night in the fort courtyard, torches flicker as the Gond Clan Chief and his elders huddle; a younger warrior gestures anxiously toward the dark horizon, where a faint distant flash suggests artillery fire.

dialogue.text: Yet this code had limits. When artillery empires pressed in from the plains, with cannons, appointed officers and written orders, the forest web was harder to tighten. Each garh had to choose when to bend or resist.

i18n.hi: फिर भी इस कोड की हद थी। जब मैदानी तोपख़ाने वाले साम्राज्य धकियाकर आए—तोपों, नियुक्त अफ़सरों और लिखित हुक्मों के साथ—तो जंगल का जाल कसना मुश्किल हुआ। हर गढ़ को तय करना पड़ा, कब झुकना, कब अड़ना।

panels.shot: medium shot of the chief listening to a scribe reading a Persian or Devanagari letter
panels.action: In a small room, a scribe in plain cloth reads from a folded paper in a script foreign to the chief; the Gond Clan Chief listens, expression guarded, fingers drumming lightly on the low table.

dialogue.text: Later documents—from Mughal officers, Maratha agents, British gazetteers—describe garhs and chaurasis in their own terms. Behind their labels we glimpse the older system, already being stretched, taxed and renamed.

i18n.hi: बाद के काग़ज़—मुग़ल अमलों, मराठा कारिंदों, अंग्रेज़ गज़ेटियरों के—अपने शब्दों में गढ़ और चौरासी लिखते हैं। उनकी मुहरों के पीछे हमें पुराना ढाँचा झलकता है, जो तब तक खिंच, taxed और नया नाम पा रहा था।

panels.shot: wide shot of a garh losing prominence as a new stone town grows nearby
panels.action: Beyond the aging hill-fort, a new stone town grows on the plain—straight streets, a mosque or temple spire, tiled roofs—while fewer fires burn on the fort’s terraces and some walls look neglected.

dialogue.text: Some garhs faded as plains towns rose. Chaurasi and barhot boundaries blurred under new revenue circles. But in village speech and clan memory, their names clung to ridges, tanks and paths long after.

i18n.hi: कुछ गढ़ मैदानी कस्बों के उभरते ही मिट गए। चौरासी और बारहट की हदें नई महसूल परगनों में धुंधली हो गईं। पर गाँव की बोली और कुलों की याद में, उनके नाम पहाड़ियों, तालों और पगडंडियों से चिपके रहे।

panels.shot: close-up of an elderly chief’s weathered face, half in shadow, looking toward forest
panels.action: An older Gond Clan Chief, hair streaked with grey, sits at the fort gate; half his face lies in shadow, the other half lit as he gazes toward the forest he once ranged as a young warrior.

dialogue.speaker: the_gond_clan_chiefs
dialogue.text: Forts fall. But as long as the forest remembers our paths, the code breathes.

i18n.hi: किले गिरते हैं। पर जब तक जंगल हमारी पगडंडियाँ याद रखे, कोड साँस लेता रहेगा।

panels.shot: wide contemplative shot of present-day central Indian landscape with faint ruins
panels.action: In a modern hazy dawn, scrub and fields sprawl around a low hill where mossy fort stones barely rise above the grass; a thin path winds past a village, a tank and a patch of forest.

dialogue.text: Today, gazetteers and historians piece together this forest code from ruins, place-names and accounts. It reminds us that good governance can grow from the land itself, fitting hills, water and people more than paper.

i18n.hi: आज गज़ेटियर और इतिहासकार इस जंगल कोड को खंडहरों, जगह-नामों और बयानों से जोड़ रहे हैं। यह दिखाता है कि अच्छी रियासत ज़मीन से भी उग सकती है, काग़ज़ से कम, और पहाड़, पानी और लोगों से ज़्यादा मेल खाती हुई।

subtitle_i18n.en: How Forts, Forests and Eighty-Four Villages Held a Kingdom Together
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे किले, जंगल और चौरासी गाँवों ने एक राज्य जोड़े रखा
